patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Motion and Office Timeline share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Motion only if your buying job matches “AI calendar + task auto-scheduling (projects, docs, meetings) — Pro AI from $19/seat/mo an” rather than Office Timeline's shape. Choose Office Timeline only if your buying job matches “PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite fro” rather than Motion's shape. Workflow advantage: Motion leans work-management; Office Timeline leans timeline-reporting. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Motion and Office Timeline share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Motion is AI calendar + task auto-scheduling (projects, docs, meetings) — Pro AI from $19/seat/mo annual.; Office Timeline is PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in; Lite from $9/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Motion (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Office Timeline (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Motion-leaning work-management vs Office Timeline-leaning timeline-reporting.
- Researched limits: Motion — Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors; Office Timeline — Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management.

Limitations — Motion: Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors; AI credit caps and top-ups affect TCO; Office Timeline: Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management; Centre of gravity is PowerPoint presentation timelines, not live team task execution.

Poor-fit cases: Motion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Premium $19+ seats vs broader Work OS floors · Office Timeline is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a work OS — no monday/Hive-class boards, automations or workload management · Avoid Motion if you actually need Office Timeline's motion (PowerPoint-native timeline / Gantt specialist (now Lucen Timeline) — Free add-in)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
